evidence.claim: The Center found a higher incidence of machine problems in the 2022 elections that were locally disruptive and also found that observed precinct procedures did not effectively ensure the secrecy of the vote.
evidence.title: Final Report: 2022 General Elections in the Philippines
evidence.excerpt: The Center found a higher incidence of machine problems in the 2022 elections that were locally disruptive and also found that observed precinct procedures did not effectively ensure the secrecy of the vote.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent technical election assessment with specific process findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly institutional/electoral-system context; relevant to Marcos's accession but not a personal action by him.
contrary_evidence: The report says the problems did not jeopardize overall integrity, so this is a mixed rather than catastrophic finding.

evidence.claim: The Carter Center said campaign-finance rules were only partly effective, with spending caps widely viewed as too low, a mostly unregulated pre-campaign period, and weak enforcement capacity at COMELEC.
evidence.title: Final Report: 2022 General Elections in the Philippines
evidence.excerpt: The Carter Center said campaign-finance rules were only partly effective, with spending caps widely viewed as too low, a mostly unregulated pre-campaign period, and weak enforcement capacity at COMELEC.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent election report with detailed legal-analysis findings.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the 2022 campaign and election cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This concerns the campaign system that enabled Marcos's victory, not a personal order by him after inauguration.
contrary_evidence: The report identifies system-wide loopholes, not necessarily a Marcos-only manipulation scheme.

evidence.claim: NAMFREL said the 2022 elections went smoothly but not without issues, and it separately recorded pockets of violence and intimidation during election day.
evidence.title: NAMFREL 2022 National and Local Elections Preliminary Report
evidence.excerpt: NAMFREL said the 2022 elections went smoothly but not without issues, and it separately recorded pockets of violence and intimidation during election day.
evidence.source_locator: report page entries dated July 18 and May 9, 2022
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major Philippine election watchdog, but the accessible page is a portal to the report summary rather than the full PDF text.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly about the election environment rather than Marcos's later conduct.
contrary_evidence: The accessible summary is limited and does not by itself resolve the full range of election disputes.

evidence.claim: The report said concerns over press freedom grew because Marcos held professional journalists in low regard during the campaign; it also said he barred journalists from campaign events, snubbed debates, and favored friendly influencers and a partisan TV station.
evidence.title: Philippines | 2022 Digital News Report
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford
evidence.excerpt: The report said concerns over press freedom grew because Marcos held professional journalists in low regard during the campaign; it also said he barred journalists from campaign events, snubbed debates, and favored friendly influencers and a partisan TV station.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent research report with direct, dated observations of campaign behavior and media environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Marcos's own campaign conduct and the surrounding information environment.
contrary_evidence: This is a media-research country note, not an election tribunal finding.

evidence.claim: CHR said red-tagging in recent years has led to vilification, surveillance, harassment, unlawful arrests, enforced disappearance, and killings, and it warned that government officials continued to resort to the practice.
evidence.title: Statement of the Commission on Human Rights on the attempt to trivialize and justify the dangers of red-tagging
evidence.excerpt: CHR said red-tagging in recent years has led to vilification, surveillance, harassment, unlawful arrests, enforced disappearance, and killings, and it warned that government officials continued to resort to the practice.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Philippine constitutional human-rights body, dated and explicit about the harms and continuing government use.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 campaign and transition period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The statement addresses state-linked practice during the Marcos transition, though not every incident is personally ordered by Marcos.
contrary_evidence: CHR is a rights-monitoring institution, so the statement is protective rather than neutral.

evidence.claim: Marcos asked Congress to pass National Government Rightsizing, Budget Modernization, E-Government, and E-Governance measures, saying they would improve service delivery, institutional capacity, and fiscal discipline.
evidence.title: PBBM urges Congress to pass admin’s 19 priority measures
evidence.excerpt: Marcos asked Congress to pass National Government Rightsizing, Budget Modernization, E-Government, and E-Governance measures, saying they would improve service delivery, institutional capacity, and fiscal discipline.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government release summarizing a first-term SONA policy program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Marcos policy agenda, though it is legislative proposal rather than enacted reform.
contrary_evidence: These are reform proposals, not completed institutional-strengthening outcomes.

evidence.claim: APHR said disinformation and red-tagging of opposition lawmakers increased alarmingly ahead of the May 2022 polls, and that Leni Robredo was the prime target of intensified disinformation and red-tagging in social media.
evidence.title: Disinformation, red-tagging of opposition lawmakers in PH 'increased alarmingly' ahead of 2022 elections - APHR
evidence.excerpt: APHR said disinformation and red-tagging of opposition lawmakers increased alarmingly ahead of the May 2022 polls, and that Leni Robredo was the prime target of intensified disinformation and red-tagging in social media.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Regional parliamentary rights network reported through a major local outlet, but it is retrospective and third-party summarized.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly about the campaign environment that benefited Marcos, not a direct post-inauguration order by him.
contrary_evidence: Retrospective and coalition-based, so it should not be treated as a direct legal finding.

evidence.claim: ACLED recorded nearly 50 red-tagging related violent events targeting civilians between 2020 and June 30, 2023, including 13 events after Marcos took power on June 30, 2022.
evidence.title: ACLED: The communist insurgency in the Philippines: A 'protracted people’s war' continues
evidence.excerpt: ACLED recorded nearly 50 red-tagging related violent events targeting civilians between 2020 and June 30, 2023, including 13 events after Marcos took power on June 30, 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Event-data organization using transparent methodology; retrospective but concrete about post-inauguration continuation.
evidence.period_fit: Spans the target year and the immediate follow-on period, so it is retrospective context rather than pure 2022 contemporaneous reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The events are not all personally ordered by Marcos, but they show continuity of the red-tagging environment after he assumed office.
contrary_evidence: The report covers a broader period than 2022 alone.

unresolved_gaps: No direct nuclear-command or crisis-use decision in 2022.
No external war or proxy-conflict record in 2022, so some conduct lenses are structurally thin.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for red-tagging and some police outcomes remains limited.
Election-year evidence is stronger on campaign behavior and information environment than on post-inauguration institutional change.
National household/distribution outcomes are better evidenced in 2023 follow-through than in clean 2022-only attribution.
Most welfare evidence is rollout or partner-supported evidence rather than a full national outcome audit.
Direct 2022 asset/SALN and office-period wealth evidence remains thin.
Agency-level execution evidence is thinner than agenda-setting and budget evidence.
